newsitem.title: INDIA: Oman's Qaboos to visit India, boost economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Oman's Qaboos to visit India, boost economic ties.

text.p: Oman's Sultan Qaboos Bin Said will visit India next week at the head of a large delegation, Oman's ambassador in New Delhi Mohammed Taher Alawi Aideed said on Thursday.
"This will be his first official visit to Asia," Alawi told reporters. "We have had Indian leaders visiting Oman so far. With this visit we will be expressing our official love for India."
He said Qaboos, Oman's head of state, will arrive on March 18 with a big delegation, including ministers and businessmen.
The two countries are members of the recently inaugurated 14-member Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation.
"It is another positive step in that direction where our two countries cannot only increase trade and investment but also reach out to Australia and the countries of the African region," Alawi said.
Oman's imports from India increased from $62.4 million in 1989 to $180 million in 1996.
India's imports from Oman rose from $12.82 million in 1991 to $27.04 million last year.
Alawi said economic reforms in India had opened opportunities for bilateral investments.

The two countries have carried out a feasibility study for a proposed underwater gas pipeline from Oman to India. But Indian officials say the project has been bogged down by a lack of political will on both sides and cash to carry it out.
